text:
[LCYC.6.1.3] **A bounded staged derivation is expressible.**
  One rule per stage, each guarded `where n.level == k` and
  emitting `level: k+1`, has every backward and re-entrant
  edge refuted by [LCYC.6.1]: the emitted literal cannot
  satisfy the guard of any stage but the next. What remains
  is a DAG across as many stages as the author wrote, so the
  derivation advances a bounded number of steps and stops.

  This does not weaken [LCYC.1.1]. The derivation's length is
  the number of rules, fixed at compile time, so it is
  bounded computation on the same terms as that clause's
  other enforcement points. It is not recursion
  ([LCYC.1.2]) — there is no rule that invokes itself — and
  nothing here admits a derivation whose length depends on
  the fact base.
